newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion judge - jury to remember oath.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion judge - jury to remember oath.

text.p: The federal judge presiding over Food Lion Inc's lawsuit against ABC and four of its producers told jurors deciding punitive damages Wednesday to recall their oath to deliberate in good faith.

"It is your duty as jurors to discuss the case with one another in an effort to reach agreement if you can do so. Each of you must decide the case for yourself, but only after full consideration of the evidence with the other members of the jury," U.S. District Judge Carlton Tilley said, repeating jury instructions he had given on Tuesday.
After deliberating four hours on Wednesday, the jury sent the judge a note indicating that one of the 12 jurors was not cooperating and asked how to proceed.
The decision to order punitive damages must be unanimous.
Tilley instructed the six men and six women to make its decision based only the evidence, follow the law as he instructed and not be influenced by sympathy or prejudice for either party.

ABC, a New York-based television network owned by Walt Disney Co, was ordered to pay $1,400 in compensatory damages ordered late last year when it was found to have committed fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty.
Food Lion, based in Salisbury, N.C., is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA and had 1996 sales of $9 billion.
The jury resumed deliberating at 3:30 p.m. EST (2030 GMT) after receiving the additional instruction from the judge.
